text:
Few environments shape a person’s experience as completely as a well-run hotel, and that has long been what draws me to hospitality. I have always been inspired by the way a hotel can turn an ordinary trip into a lasting memory, and that interest grew into a clear commitment to a career focused on creating welcoming, seamless guest experiences. Over time, I came to value not only the guest-facing side of hospitality, but also the coordination behind it: the timing, communication, and attention to detail that allow both guests and staff to thrive. That is why I am pursuing a path as a Hotel Manager, where I can combine service, leadership, and daily operational oversight to create a calm, polished atmosphere and build lasting guest loyalty.

I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and that academic training strengthened my ability to work in a structured, consistent way while keeping sight of practical outcomes. In one project with a tangible outcome, I had to work with a new tool and subject area, and within a few months of focused effort I was contributing confidently enough for the work to move forward on schedule. In a team setting, I also dealt with a recurring issue that had been slowing progress down; instead of letting it continue, I put in place a practical workaround that reduced delays and helped the group keep momentum. Over time, colleagues would sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I valued being able to help them think through the next step clearly.

Originally from the Netherlands, I bring an international perspective alongside a strong personal connection to hospitality. During a family stay at a sister property, my relatives began pointing out small service touches they recognised from stories I had shared, turning the trip into a light-hearted “hotel manager’s eye” challenge. Seeing them notice the care behind each detail reminded me how meaningful thoughtful hospitality can be, both professionally and personally. I am now eager to bring my education, practical mindset, and commitment to guest experience into a Hotel Manager role where I can continue learning, contribute to high standards across operations, and help create stays that guests remember for the right reasons.

Few fields hold my attention like marketing, because I have always been fascinated by what makes people notice a message, remember it, and act on it. That curiosity grew into a clear career direction as I saw how marketing brings together creativity, psychology, and business impact, and how strong campaigns can connect audience needs with meaningful brand stories. I am originally from Germany, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through my studies and project work, I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in building campaigns that are both imaginative and grounded in evidence. What keeps me energized is shaping work that strengthens brand presence and supports measurable growth by turning customer insight and performance data into clear campaign decisions.

Currently, I am focused on building my career as a Marketing Manager, drawing on both formal training and practical experience. In one recent area of work, I needed to use a new analytics and campaign management tool that was unfamiliar to me; after a few months of focused effort, I was using it confidently in day-to-day tasks and applying its reporting features to support campaign decisions. In project settings, I handle routine issues by working through established processes, whether that means checking campaign timelines, reviewing performance figures against agreed benchmarks, or following approval steps carefully, and when an unusual case falls outside those patterns, I make a point of seeking guidance so the work stays accurate and on track. I also enjoy working alongside colleagues; for example, when teammates have asked how I approached audience segmentation or organised reporting updates, I have talked them through my process and shared the materials I was using.

One moment that made this career feel especially real came at a weekend market, when my family noticed a display from a campaign I had helped launch and excitedly pointed out the tagline in the middle of everyday life. It was funny, rewarding, and a reminder of why this profession matters to me. Looking ahead, I want to continue growing as a Marketing Manager and contribute to campaigns that are thoughtful, effective, and closely connected to the audiences they serve.

Few roles matter more than being present when someone is facing crisis, uncertainty, or a major life transition. That is what drew me to social work: a deep belief that timely support and compassionate advocacy can change the course of someone’s life, and a commitment to helping individuals and families navigate complex systems with dignity, hope, and practical support. My connection to this profession became especially clear at a community event linked to my work, when a relative quietly told me they finally understood why I care so much about social work after watching a family I had supported stop to say thank you. Moments like that confirmed for me that this is not simply employment, but work I want to keep building my life around. Originally from Spain, I bring that sense of purpose to every setting in which I work.

My academic development has given me a strong foundation for this path. I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and through my studies I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of turning assessment and planning into practical results for people. This led me to keep expanding my understanding of how support systems work in practice and how person-centred decisions can be sustained over time. In one role, I needed to use a new digital case-management tool and, after a few months of focused effort, I was handling day-to-day tasks confidently enough for it to become part of my regular workflow. On another occasion, repeated delays in sharing updates across the team were affecting response times, so I introduced a simple tracking method that gave everyone one place to check progress and reduced the disruption the issue had been causing.

In addition, my day-to-day work has shown me how much effective support depends on trust, calm communication, and practical follow-through. Colleagues have sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, particularly when they wanted a second view on how to approach a case or explain a process clearly to a service user. Although my interest began with a belief in advocacy and care, experiences like these have expanded my perspective on what good social work requires in practice. Consequently, I am keen to bring my commitment, judgement, and person-centred approach to a Social Worker role where I can continue supporting people in meaningful, well-coordinated ways.

Few roles reward genuine human connection as directly as sales, and that is what continues to draw me to a career as a Sales Representative. I have always been energized by meeting new people, understanding what matters to them, and helping them find the right solution, so sales became a natural path for me. What keeps me engaged is the chance to turn conversations into trust by identifying customer needs quickly and presenting solutions in a way that feels personal, clear, and valuable. That approach matters to me because it supports long-term client relationships, strong retention, and repeat business. My perspective on professional communication was shaped further through doctoral study at a university ranked in the global top 500, where I learned that progress often depends on asking the right questions, listening carefully, and explaining complex points in a way others can use. This encouraged me to approach customer conversations more thoughtfully, focusing not only on what is being asked but also on what will be most useful to the person in front of me.

Following this, I carried that mindset into practical work and completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, each of which reinforced the value of clear goals and steady follow-through. In one role, I needed to use a new tool that was central to tracking activity and reporting; after a few months of focused effort, I was using it confidently in my daily work and contributing productively to the team’s routine processes. In day-to-day situations, I work through issues by following established procedures, and when an unusual case falls outside those steps, I make sure to seek guidance so the customer receives the right outcome. I also work well alongside colleagues; for example, when a teammate asked how I was structuring follow-up conversations with returning clients, I walked them through my approach so they could adapt it for their own accounts. Originally from France, I bring that same commitment to every interaction. At a community event I was attending for work, my family stopped by and spoke with one of my long-time clients, who laughed that they finally understood why I am always remembered by name. That moment captured exactly why this work feels meaningful to me, and why I am excited to contribute that energy, care, and consistency to a new sales team.

Precision has always appealed to me because laboratory work turns careful testing into results that matter well beyond the bench. What draws me most to a Laboratory Technician role is the way accurate, methodical work supports wider scientific and healthcare goals, whether in research, quality processes, or patient outcomes. I am originally from the Netherlands, and I hold a Doctorate from a university not listed in the major global rankings. During that academic path, I completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, and those experiences showed me how much I value producing dependable results that others can use with confidence. That connection to the work is personal as well as professional: one of my favourite family memories is coming home after a busy week in the lab and discovering that my younger sibling had turned the kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples. It was a funny moment, but also a reminder that my enthusiasm for methodical work and discovery is something my family can see and share.

A project during my doctorate broadened my perspective on laboratory work by showing me how much progress depends on consistency at every stage, from sample preparation to recording results clearly enough for others to act on them. In one period of focused work, I needed to use a new laboratory tool and became productive with it within a few months by setting aside regular time to practise, compare outputs, and refine my routine until I could use it confidently in day-to-day tasks. In daily lab work, I handle routine problems by following established procedures carefully, and when an unusual case falls outside those steps, I make a point of checking with a more experienced colleague before proceeding. Colleagues have also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, particularly when they wanted a second pair of eyes on a process or documentation detail. I am motivated to continue developing as a Laboratory Technician, bringing genuine curiosity, careful testing, and consistent documentation to a role where reliable work behind the scenes can make a real difference.

Movement first became personal to me during a family holiday, when a relative recovering from a minor injury asked for help with a few simple mobility exercises and, before long, the whole family had joined in for an impromptu stretching session before breakfast. That funny moment stayed with me because it showed how recovery, support, and confidence in movement can grow together. Growing up in Spain, I was drawn to physiotherapy by a genuine interest in how the body heals and adapts, combined with the satisfaction of helping people regain confidence in their movement and daily lives. For me, it is a career that blends science, empathy, and practical problem-solving in a way that creates visible, meaningful progress. Through my studies and research at a university ranked in the global top 100, culminating in a Doctorate, I deepened that interest and learned how careful clinical assessment can be translated into highly personalized rehabilitation plans that patients can follow with purpose and motivation.

In particular, while working on one of the 7 completed projects with tangible outcomes, I needed to use a new assessment and data-analysis tool that was unfamiliar to the team; within a few weeks I was using it confidently in practice, and soon afterwards I was showing colleagues how to set it up and apply it in their own work. On another project, I faced a rehabilitation planning problem that several people had been unable to resolve, so I designed a different framework for combining assessment findings with staged treatment goals; it was later taken up beyond my own team. Beyond this, colleagues and supervisors regularly came to me with difficult questions, including issues outside my immediate area, such as interpreting complex case information or refining project decisions under time pressure.

Alongside building knowledge, these experiences strengthened my communication, organisation, and collaborative working. Overall, with a Doctorate, experience gained at a university ranked in the global top 100, and 7 completed projects with tangible outcomes, I am prepared to bring a thoughtful and practical approach to a Physiotherapist role, helping patients make steady progress toward recovery, independence, and long-term wellbeing.

Few parts of a business are remembered as clearly as the moment a customer needs help, and that is why I have built my career direction around customer service leadership. I am from France, and I was drawn to this path by the challenge of turning stressful moments into positive outcomes and by the satisfaction of helping both customers and team members feel heard, supported, and confident. One of my favourite family stories captures that connection perfectly: a relative once called my workplace without realising I was the supervisor handling the escalation, and by the end of the conversation they laughed and said, “Now I understand why everyone asks for the manager.” That light-hearted moment stayed with me because it showed how patience, clarity, and care can shape trust in every interaction.

My academic background includes a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, where I completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes. Working through those projects gave me experience of taking structured ideas through to practical results, and during that period I also became productive with a new tool within a few months of focused effort so that I could contribute properly to the work required. Alongside formal study, I became increasingly interested in how service teams can stay calm, empathetic, and solution-focused in high-pressure situations, and how recurring customer concerns can be turned into practical process improvements that support both satisfaction and performance standards.

In day-to-day work, I am comfortable handling routine issues by following established procedures carefully, and when an unusual case falls outside those steps, I make sure to seek guidance early so the customer receives the right outcome. I also work well alongside colleagues; for example, when a teammate asked how I was tracking repeated customer queries, I showed them the approach I was using so they could apply it in their own cases. Although my interest began with individual customer interactions, it has grown into a clear commitment to supervising service teams, and consequently I am eager to bring this combination of study, practical judgement, and genuine enthusiasm to a Customer Service Supervisor role.

What keeps me committed to hotel management is the chance to turn ordinary travel into something memorable, creating spaces where people feel genuinely welcomed while ensuring everything behind the scenes runs smoothly. That combination of hospitality, problem-solving, and operational focus is what drew me to this profession, and it continues to shape the way I approach service. I am originally from France, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through that academic journey, and through completing 4 projects with tangible outcomes, I developed a disciplined approach to planning, analysis, and delivery that I now bring to guest experience and hotel operations. This has confirmed my desire to build a career leading teams that can provide warm, high-standard service while maintaining efficiency across the whole property.

In practice, I have often been the person colleagues and supervisors turn to when a difficult question needs answering, including questions outside my own area; in one role, team members from different functions would come to me during busy periods to help untangle booking, process, and coordination issues so service could continue without disruption. When a new system was introduced, I became proficient with it within a few weeks and soon afterwards helped others get started, showing them how to use it confidently in their day-to-day work. I also designed an original solution to a problem that others had not managed to solve, and after it proved effective, it was adopted beyond my own team. Alongside work, I value the human side of hospitality deeply. On a family weekend visit to one of my properties, my team quietly helped coordinate a surprise wedding proposal in the lobby, and my family still tells the story as though we were all part of the event team. For me, that moment captured exactly why this career matters: hotels are not only places to stay, but places where important memories are made. I am ready to bring that perspective, energy, and commitment to a Hotel Manager role.

Few roles make such an immediate difference as nursing, and that is what continues to draw me to work as a Registered Nurse. I chose this profession because I want to comfort people during their most vulnerable moments and support both patients and their families through recovery, uncertainty, and hope. That purpose became even more personal during a community health event when a family member visited my workplace and joked that I seemed to know everyone in the room; seeing how a few calm words and genuine care could put strangers at ease reminded me why this work matters so much to me. My academic path has also shaped how I practise: I am from Germany, I hold a Doctorate, and I studied at a university ranked in the global top 100. This showed me the value of combining careful thinking with practical action, and in clinical settings it has led me to pay close attention to small changes in a patient’s condition so that care can be adjusted promptly and clearly communicated to relatives and the wider team.

In practice, I have developed through situations that demanded steady learning and problem-solving. When my team introduced a new digital documentation system, I set aside focused time over several months to learn it thoroughly and was soon using it confidently in daily work, helping maintain accurate records and continuity of care. On another occasion, repeated delays in locating key discharge information were slowing the ward, so I created a simple handover and checklist process that made the information easier to find and reduced disruption for colleagues and patients. I have completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of organisation, communication, and follow-through. Colleagues and supervisors now regularly come to me with difficult questions, including issues outside my own area, such as clarifying documentation pathways or helping think through next steps in unfamiliar cases. Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of practical care, thoughtful judgement, teamwork, and commitment to patient wellbeing to my next Registered Nurse role.

Meaningful sales begins with understanding what matters to people and helping them find solutions that genuinely make their work or lives easier. That belief is what drew me to a career as a Sales Representative, and it continues to shape the way I approach every conversation: by listening carefully, asking the right questions, and turning customer needs into clear value. My interest in this path deepened through seeing how strong client relationships are built over time, not in a single pitch but through consistent, thoughtful communication. Looking ahead, I want to keep building a career in sales where I can turn conversations into long-term relationships and contribute to results that customers remember positively.

I am originally from the Netherlands and hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100. My academic background gave me a structured way of thinking, and I have applied that mindset through three completed projects with tangible outcomes, each of which required me to move from ideas to practical delivery. For example, when I needed to work with a new tool outside my usual experience, I set aside focused time each week and, within a few months, was using it confidently enough to contribute productively to project work. In another team setting, a recurring issue was slowing progress, so I mapped where delays were happening and introduced a simple workaround that reduced the bottleneck and helped the team keep moving. Through this, I saw how practical solutions can make an immediate difference.

Colleagues have also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, particularly when they wanted a second view on how to approach a task or explain something more clearly. Beyond formal experience, one moment that stays with me came at a community event hosted by one of my clients, where my family spoke with customers who warmly described how much they appreciated the service I had helped deliver. Seeing my family’s pride in that moment reinforced why this profession matters to me: sales is not only about closing deals, but about creating trust, value, and positive experiences that last.
